body:
Minutes:

- PR 12860 Module Stylesheets Syntax: Kurt Catti-Schmidt presented PR 12860 regarding module stylesheets, proposing a new `import` attribute (e.g., `import="foo"`) instead of `type="module"` to handle import map-aware fetches without breaking existing MIME type filtering on the `link` tag ([00:00:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.3udzvxvn3p43)). Emilio Cobos Álvarez and Ryosuke Niwa raised questions regarding consistency with script elements, where `type="module"` is utilized ([00:05:26](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.s9ej0n56w3o7)). Simon Pieters and Anne van Kesteren discussed legacy script type usages and fallback behaviors, noting that an unknown attribute fails open ([00:06:29](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.wqze9p6xazvt)) ([00:09:50](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.1ymxjy9wb9ws)). Kurt Catti-Schmidt noted that the `import` attribute is less verbose and more extensible to other tags ([00:11:21](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.l2nsemgdvkq)). Ryosuke Niwa suggested continuing the discussion asynchronously on GitHub and the PR ([00:12:23](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.3t64oxcdycrz)).
- Issue 662 Custom Elements Callback Promise: Johnny Stenback noted that issue 662 regarding custom elements callback promises for connected and parsed could not be discussed because Keith was absent from the meeting ([00:13:20](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.lcw0quko0cj)).
- Issue 12388 Spell Check Custom Dictionary: Brian Kardell requested to advance issue 12388 for a spell check custom dictionary to stage two, noting that the proposal received initial accessibility and internationalization feedback ([00:13:20](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.lcw0quko0cj)). Olli Pettay expressed neutrality and a concern that the API might see low usage due to future AI spellcheckers. Brian Kardell, Luke, and Mason Freed argued that AI cannot recognize domain-specific, fantasy, or fictional words (such as in *Lord of the Rings* or custom games) without explicit context or custom dictionaries ([00:14:35](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.i6h5ddqk1o08)). With support from Mason Freed and Olli Pettay's neutrality, Johnny Stenback agreed to mark the issue as advancing to stage two ([00:16:59](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.gwhc04fe816e)).
- Issue 10650 HTML and Canvas Overview and Stage Three Request: Philip Rogers presented an overview of issue 10650 regarding HTML in canvas, noting that 47% of page views use canvas elements and 15% draw text, requiring the reimplementation of features like text selection and accessibility ([00:18:00](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.xql01gmsfxxu)). The proposal allows exposing HTML in a canvas subtree to solve these issues, showing high developer interest and partner usage from Figma. Philip Rogers requested stage three status for the API, stating that the processing model is fully described and tested ([00:19:42](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.1ml2y0rn8to8)).
- Issue 10650 HTML and Canvas Review and Approval: Said Abou-Hallawa stated that WebKit supports implementing the feature and has started working on it. Anne van Kesteren raised questions regarding video rendering issues being resolved, which Philip Jägenstedt confirmed, and noted that the attribute was renamed to `content=drawable` or `content=fallback` ([00:22:02](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.kkv4ghhemwxj)). Anne van Kesteren also expressed concern over the lack of external review, but Philip Jägenstedt and Stefan Zager reassured the group regarding spec maintenance and testing quality ([00:23:07](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.wn9n6stveoo9)). With WebKit indicating support through Said Abou-Hallawa and Anne van Kesteren, the group agreed to advance the HTML and canvas proposal to stage three ([00:29:12](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.s6v2uevtgg4w)).
- Issue 11729 Menu Elements Proposal and Checkable Syntax: David Baron (David Baron) requested stage three for issue 11729 regarding menu elements and discussed open design points regarding checkable menu items ([00:30:34](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.khghdld1gm9y)). David Baron proposed using `checkable="single"` or `checkable="multiple"` on the menu item element, with grouping determined by the nearest ancestor `fieldset`, `menulist`, or `menubar` ([00:34:02](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.egeaktjyreqi)). Olli Pettay expressed a preference for simpler syntax without requiring a `fieldset` everywhere, and Luke questioned whether `menuitemcheckbox` and `menuitemradio` elements would be clearer ([00:32:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.fwvvz4huwb1i)) ([00:36:17](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.ui8l0ptiwxiq)). David Baron and Olli Pettay debated terminology and rendering conventions, noting that platforms like macOS and Google Docs use check marks for both types, whereas Linux and other applications use distinct radio rendering ([00:37:44](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.xp81itqr4qx0)). Luke and Emilio Cobos Álvarez also discussed user agent stylesheets and consistency with select element appearances ([00:39:57](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.4s9rt5s3pj63)).
- Issue 11729 Menu Elements Stage Three Evaluation: Mason Freed advocated for moving the menu elements proposal to stage three to drive detailed specification reviews, while Anne van Kesteren argued against stage three advancement because the API shape and naming decisions are not yet fully stabilized ([00:42:33](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.u0a4y5hn4esh)). Philip Jägenstedt and Olli Pettay noted that while the overall proposal looks good, the specific checkable syntax needs resolution ([00:45:07](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.pml201bzwi5l)). Johnny Stenback concluded that the group should resolve the syntax issue further before moving to stage three, keeping the item on the agenda ([00:46:17](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.b27hb74bao84)).
- Stephanie Zhang Opaque Range PR Update: Stephanie Zhang provided a brief update on the opaque range proposal, requesting a fresh round of reviews on the pull request ([00:46:17](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.b27hb74bao84)). Anne van Kesteren noted that the pull request did not previously reflect the agreed-upon design and omitted fake offset details, but Stephanie Zhang explained that this was due to a poor rebase and that the changes had just been restored ([00:47:23](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.qulpa6o52qeo)).
- Meeting Scheduling and Timezone Discussion: Olli Pettay noted that Mozilla participants will be in Toronto next week, causing a scheduling conflict for the European-friendly slot ([00:47:23](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.qulpa6o52qeo)). This prompted a broader discussion led by Philip Jägenstedt, Anne van Kesteren, Simon Pieters, and David Baron regarding meeting schedules, timezone rotations, and dissatisfaction with frequent evening meetings for European participants ([00:48:35](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.jlza2zh4w1wp)) ([00:54:33](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.9qxdajefuf1f)). Stefan Zager suggested defining fixed time slots for topics to help participants joining at difficult hours ([00:51:31](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.d85rrlmm1rqc)). The group agreed to discuss and propose alternative scheduling options during the following week's meeting ([00:53:01](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.o7kcvuflkkgo)) ([00:55:35](https://docs.google.com/document/d/141R9ofg5-KwkTC0JWFMpP9uj4GlcLe4u04JX1mj4Mx0/edit?userstoinvite=none&tab=t.xz2bsh5bcyl8#heading=h.kedidmmswbft)).
